---
title: "The agent context & collaboration system"
subtitle: "Shared context, review notes, and tools for any agent"
---

Flux gives agents access to the same project files and editing tools as the app. Run
an agent in your preferred terminal or vendor app, give it the project's context, and
ask it to compose figures, write prose, or address your review notes.

The files carry the context between sessions. Your machine's `UserContext` folder
holds your background and standing rules; each project's `Context` folder holds its
background and links, an append-only Log, and project rules. The Flux app is the review surface alongside the
agent: figures, manuscripts, comments, and context-stamped feedback.

# Where everything lives

Run `flux config` for this machine's resolved paths.

**Machine level — `<FluxConfig>/`:**

| Path | What | Who writes |
|---|---|---|
| `Context/UserContext/` | `WHO-AM-I.md` (you) + `RULES.md` (your standing rules) + any files you add | **You** |
| `Context/FluxContext/` | The stock docs — the single canonical home of agent-facing Flux knowledge (doctrine, workflow, every verb, slides, python/uv conventions, Lighttable…). Re-synced on every Flux update with machine paths baked in. | **Flux** |
| `plot_library/` | Your **global plot library**: reusable plots (any folders) that every project's Plot gallery can insert under **Global**. `flux config` reports it as `plotLibraryPath`. | **You** (and agents you ask) |

**Project level — `<project>/Context/`** (scaffolded for new projects; healed into old
ones when standard files are missing, on open or via `flux context-init`; `project.json` is required):

| Path | What | Who writes |
|---|---|---|
| `ProjectContext.qmd` | Background, goals if any, data/code, and links every connected agent should read | You have final say |
| `NOTEBOOK.md` | The append-only **Log**, newest last | You, or an agent **when you ask** |
| `RULES.md` | Your standing project rules; agents may propose additions | **You** |

ProjectContext, notebook, and rules are **first-class Flux Paper documents** — they appear in
the document picker's Context group, and **margin comments work on them**: annotate your
agent's understanding or memory and it treats those threads as corrections. The
feedback ledger and provenance journal live in `.meta/`.

ProjectContext is the place to put background an agent keeps missing. Link plans, data notes,
and other must-read files there; connected agents read those links too.

Ask an agent to log work when you want it recorded. `flux log` adds a dated entry with an
automatic agent · surface · host:cwd byline (the model name you pass, plus the product Flux detects). `flux read-log` reads entries; a requested
checkpoint summarizes earlier work without deleting it, so agents can catch up from the
latest checkpoint while the full history remains available.

Project-root `AGENTS.md` suggests connecting through flux-connect only when asked.
`CLAUDE.md` contains `@AGENTS.md`, so Claude Code reads the same pointer. Existing user-written
files are preserved. Older project layouts need the one-shot migration script; opening an
unmigrated project adds missing standard files without renaming old ones.

Your `Context/UserContext/Skills/` folder holds one `<name>/SKILL.md` per skill, with
`name` and `description` front matter. Its seeded README describes the format and publishing
to your agents.

# The review loop (in the app)

- **Margin comments** anchor a discussion to document text.
- **Ctrl+Shift+M** opens **Annotate** in Figure, Paper, Slide, Library, Reader, Present,
  and utility windows. Your current selection becomes a target chip. Type immediately:
  the note keeps keystrokes even while the frozen view is being captured.
- **Annotate…** is also in the global and Paper palettes and Library's **Commands…** menu.
- In Reader, select PDF text or open a saved highlight and click **✦ Annotate this passage**
  to prefill a passage target.

## Connect an agent

Run `flux connect setup --dry-run` to preview agent setup, then `flux connect setup`
to install the flux-connect skill and user-scope MCP registration for detected
Claude Code and Codex installations. Use `--agents claude,codex` to choose them,
`--yes` to confirm replacement of an existing Flux registration, and
`--use-this-install` to select this Flux installation as the launcher's owner.
Restart open agent sessions afterward. Setup backs up changed files and preserves
unmanaged skills and unrelated Claude MCP servers.

Invoke `/flux-connect <project>` in Claude Code or `$flux-connect <project>` in
Codex when you want to connect. The skill only runs on an explicit request.
Setup also installs a prompt-submit refresh hook. In Codex, review and trust it
through `/hooks`; if that Codex version lacks hooks, MCP refresh remains available.

Place personal skills in `FluxConfig/Context/UserContext/Skills/<name>/SKILL.md`,
with YAML `name` matching the folder and a nonempty `description`. Setup publishes
these to connected vendors as symlinks, so edits are live. Windows installations
without symlink privileges use managed copies. Opening Flux or running its CLI
resyncs copies and unpublishes deleted skills. Name collisions and edited vendor
copies are preserved and reported by `flux connect doctor`.

Use `flux connect doctor --json` for structured diagnostics, or `flux connect remove
--agents codex --yes` to disconnect a vendor. Removal restores replaced registration
content while preserving unrelated changes. The shared Flux launcher stays installed.

## Point, type, add {#sec-annotate}

The frozen view fills the window, with drawing tools at the top left and a focused note
at the bottom right. Hover to see the target's outline and name: a plot series, text box,
figure, caption, paragraph, slide, animation clip, PDF passage, or reference.

**Drag** to draw a numbered arrow. **Alt+A**, **Alt+B**, and **Alt+P** select arrow, box,
and pen. An arrow names its tip's target; a box names the objects inside; a pen names its
starting target. **Alt+Z** undoes a mark. Use **Alt+↑ / ↓** or the wheel to widen/narrow the
hovered target; each chip also has widening and remove controls.

**Enter** adds the annotation; **Shift+Enter** inserts a newline. **Escape** or the chord
again closes the surface and keeps the draft and its picture. **Attach view** is on by
default and remembered; drawing marks forces it on. The saved picture is cropped around
marks, or captures the whole window when there are none. If capture is unavailable, the
note still carries targets and marks and tells you there is no screenshot.

If the view changed while a draft was closed, its earlier picture and targets stay together.
Choose **Refresh view (clears marks)** to keep the note and draw on the current view.

## To: choose who receives it

**Inbox** is the default: collect notes until you ask an agent to address them. **Any
watching agent** lets the first watching session claim the item. Choose a connected agent
by name to queue the annotation for that session. Agents that are connected but not watching
are greyed and marked **queued until it watches**. Your choice is remembered per project.

**Tab** in the note cycles recipients. Typing **@any** or **@heron** also sets **To:**;
recognized routing mentions are removed from the saved text. **#tags** appear as chips.
Background-agent routing is not yet available; choose Inbox or a connected session.

## Pair with the live window

Connect with `--live` to pair with the open project. A connected session in live mode
shows **Pairing** in Annotate's **To:** menu; choose its name to hand it an annotation.
An agent can use `get_view` to see the current Flux window and its context, including
while Annotate is open. Each view briefly shows **◉ heron viewed your window** in the
titlebar, using that session's name.

**Settings → General → Allow agents to view the Flux window** is on by default.
Turn it off to refuse agent screenshots. The agent receives a clear disabled message.
Viewing captures only that project's Flux window.

## Queued: Edit, Withdraw, and status {#sec-note-popover}

Expand **Queued** to review annotations. **Edit** loads the original text, targets, and
picture; **Add** replaces that annotation while preserving its history. **Withdraw** removes
it from the active queue. The ledger is append-only at `.meta/feedback.ndjson`; pictures live
in `.meta/feedback/`. A picture is saved before its note is published.

Status chips update as agents work: **Queued → heron**, **Claimed by heron**, **heron needs
your input**, and **Resolved by heron**. Toasts name the agent. A question's toast opens the
annotation and its replies. You can reassign an item or release its claim from the queued list.

# Design properties

- **Agent-agnostic**: context lives in plain files, and CLI/MCP tools expose the edits.
- **Durable**: notes and resolutions append to the feedback ledger.
- **Auditable**: the journal and notebook record work and its rationale.
- **Safe with several writers**: Log entries go through `flux log`,
  which appends under the same lock the app holds while you edit. Concurrent agents
  cannot overwrite each other's entries, and an agent write defers to your in-app edit.
- **Reusable preferences**: when you state a standing preference, an agent can propose
  adding it to `Context/RULES.md` for future sessions.

# Troubleshooting

- `flux: command not found` → `~/.local/bin` missing or off PATH (the shim installs
  there on first run); the full path always works — see [Installing Flux](../installation.qmd).
- A verb says `deferred: … is locked` → you're mid-edit in the app; the agent retries.
  That's the coexistence model working.
- Old project without `Context/` → open it once in the app, or `flux context-init`.
